```
module savings.schedule
  purpose: Print a yearly savings schedule with compound interest, exact to the cent.

import std.console
import std.environment

public type AppError is one of
  purpose: The ways the program can fail.
  BadUsage(detail: Text)
end

public function next_balance(balance: Decimal, percent: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Add one year of interest to a balance, rounded to the cent.
  tags: money, interest
  example: next_balance(balance: 100.00, percent: 5.00) is 105.00
  example: next_balance(balance: 105.00, percent: 5.00) is 110.25

  let interest be balance * percent / 100
  return (balance + interest).rounded(2)
end

public function yearly_lines(start: Decimal, percent: Decimal, years: Integer)
  returns List of Text
  purpose: Build one text line per year showing the balance at year end.
  tags: money, interest
  see also: next_balance
  example: yearly_lines(start: 100.00, percent: 5.00, years: 2) is ["Year 1: 105.00", "Year 2: 110.25"]

  let mutable balance be start
  let mutable lines: List of Text be []
  for each year in from 1 to years
    set balance to next_balance(balance: balance, percent: percent)
    set lines to lines.append("Year {year}: {balance}")
  end
  return lines
end

public function main() or fails with AppError
  needs console, environment
  purpose: Read start amount, yearly percent and years from the command line and print the schedule.

  let args be environment.arguments()
  if args.length() is not 3 then
    fail with BadUsage(detail: "usage: savings START PERCENT YEARS")
  end
  let start_text be args.at(0) otherwise fail with BadUsage(detail: "missing start amount")
  let percent_text be args.at(1) otherwise fail with BadUsage(detail: "missing yearly percent")
  let years_text be args.at(2) otherwise fail with BadUsage(detail: "missing number of years")
  let start be start_text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadUsage(detail: "start amount is not a number")
  let percent be percent_text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadUsage(detail: "percent is not a number")
  let years be years_text.to_integer() otherwise fail with BadUsage(detail: "years is not a whole number")
  if years is less than 0 then
    fail with BadUsage(detail: "years must not be negative")
  end

  console.print("Start: {start.rounded(2)} at {percent}% for {years} years")
  for each line in yearly_lines(start: start, percent: percent, years: years)
    console.print(line)
  end
end
```

```
module savings.schedule
  purpose: Print a yearly savings schedule with compound interest, exact to the cent.

import std.console
import std.environment

public type AppError is one of
  purpose: The ways the command line can be wrong.
  BadArguments(detail: Text)
end

public function next_balance(balance: Decimal, rate: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Add one year of interest at a yearly percentage rate, rounded to the cent.
  tags: savings, money
  example: next_balance(balance: 1000.00, rate: 5.0) is 1050.00
  example: next_balance(balance: 100.00, rate: 10.0) is 110.00

  let interest be balance * rate / 100
  return (balance + interest).rounded(2)
end

public function balances(start: Decimal, rate: Decimal, years: Integer)
  returns List of Decimal
  purpose: List the balance at the end of each year, compounding yearly.
  tags: savings, money
  see also: next_balance
  example: balances(start: 100.00, rate: 10.0, years: 2) is [110.00, 121.00]
  example: balances(start: 100.00, rate: 10.0, years: 0) is []

  let mutable current be start
  let mutable result: List of Decimal be []
  repeat until result.length() is at least years
    set current to next_balance(balance: current, rate: rate)
    set result to result.append(current)
  end
  return result
end

function parse_decimal(text: Text, name: Text)
  returns Decimal
  or fails with AppError
  purpose: Read a decimal number from a command-line argument.

  let value be text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with BadArguments(detail: "{name} must be a number")
  return value
end

function parse_years(text: Text)
  returns Integer
  or fails with AppError
  purpose: Read a whole number of years from a command-line argument.

  let value be text.to_integer() otherwise fail with BadArguments(detail: "years must be a whole number")
  if value is less than 0 then
    fail with BadArguments(detail: "years must not be negative")
  end
  return value
end

public function main() or fails with AppError
  needs console, environment
  purpose: Print the yearly balance schedule for the amount, rate and years given on the command line.

  let arguments be environment.arguments()
  if arguments.length() is not 3 then
    fail with BadArguments(detail: "usage: amount rate_percent years")
  end
  let amount_text be arguments.at(0) otherwise fail with BadArguments(detail: "missing amount")
  let rate_text be arguments.at(1) otherwise fail with BadArguments(detail: "missing rate")
  let years_text be arguments.at(2) otherwise fail with BadArguments(detail: "missing years")
  let start be parse_decimal(text: amount_text, name: "amount") otherwise fail
  let rate be parse_decimal(text: rate_text, name: "rate") otherwise fail
  let years be parse_years(years_text) otherwise fail

  console.print("Year    Balance")
  console.print("{"0".pad_left(4)}    {start}")
  let mutable year be 0
  for each balance in balances(start: start, rate: rate, years: years)
    set year to year + 1
    console.print("{year.to_text().pad_left(4)}    {balance}")
  end
end
```

```
module savings.schedule
  purpose: Print a yearly savings schedule with compound interest, exact to the cent.

import std.console
import std.environment

public type AppError is one of
  purpose: The ways the program can fail.
  Usage(detail: Text)
end

public function interest_for(balance: Decimal, rate: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: Interest earned in one year at a yearly rate in percent, rounded to the cent.
  tags: money, interest
  example: interest_for(balance: 1000.00, rate: 5.00) is 50.00
  example: interest_for(balance: 100.00, rate: 2.50) is 2.50

  return (balance * rate / 100.00).rounded(2)
end

public function next_balance(balance: Decimal, rate: Decimal)
  returns Decimal
  purpose: The balance after one more year of compound interest.
  tags: money, interest
  see also: interest_for
  example: next_balance(balance: 1000.00, rate: 5.00) is 1050.00
  example: next_balance(balance: 100.00, rate: 2.50) is 102.50

  return balance + interest_for(balance: balance, rate: rate)
end

public function main() or fails with AppError
  needs console, environment
  purpose: Read the start amount, yearly rate in percent and years, then print the yearly schedule.

  let arguments be environment.arguments()
  let start_text be arguments.at(0) otherwise fail with Usage(detail: "missing start amount")
  let rate_text be arguments.at(1) otherwise fail with Usage(detail: "missing yearly rate in percent")
  let years_text be arguments.at(2) otherwise fail with Usage(detail: "missing number of years")
  let start be start_text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with Usage(detail: "start amount is not a number")
  let rate be rate_text.to_decimal() otherwise fail with Usage(detail: "rate is not a number")
  let years be years_text.to_integer() otherwise fail with Usage(detail: "years is not a whole number")

  let mutable balance be start.rounded(2)
  console.print("Year  Balance")
  console.print("{"0".pad_left(4)}  {balance}")
  for each year in from 1 to years
    set balance to next_balance(balance: balance, rate: rate)
    console.print("{year.to_text().pad_left(4)}  {balance}")
  end
end
```
